turns.thought:
Good catch — thanks for the detail. Yes, let's handle it in that order, and don't worry, this is all safe and reversible.

**Step 1 — Turn Airplane Mode OFF first.**
Airplane Mode disables every wireless radio in the phone, including the cellular one. Turn it off (Settings → toggle Airplane Mode off, or swipe down to the quick settings panel and tap the airplane icon).

That alone may be the whole problem — with no cellular radio running, the phone can't read the SIM at all, which can make it report "No SIM card detected."

**Step 2 — Re-check the SIM status.**
Once Airplane Mode is off, check the SIM status again on the phone. If it now shows the SIM as **Active/Ready**, you're done — no need to touch the hardware at all.

**Step 3 — Only if it still says "No SIM card detected," reseat the SIM.**
This is the standard fix and doesn't damage anything:
1. Power the phone off completely.
2. Use the SIM eject tool (or a small paperclip) to gently pop open the SIM tray.
3. Take the SIM card out, check it for obvious dirt or damage, wipe it gently with a dry cloth, and place it back flat in the tray in the correct orientation.
4. Push the tray fully back in until it sits flush.
5. Power the phone back on.

**Step 4 — Reboot the device after the change.**
A full restart lets both the SIM and the roaming/data changes I made on the line take effect.

Good news on the account side: your line 555-123-2002 is **Active** (not suspended), roaming is enabled, and the 2 GB is added — so once the phone can read the SIM and connect while you're in France, MMS should work. Make sure mobile data is enabled too when the radio comes back up.

A few things to watch for:
- If after reseating the SIM still shows as **missing/not detected**, don't keep opening the tray repeatedly — tell me.
- If it shows **Locked** (asking for a PIN or PUK), stop and tell me — that needs to be escalated to technical support, since entering it incorrectly can permanently lock the card.

Go ahead with step 1 and let me know what the status bar and SIM show afterward.

Go to Settings → Network/Connections → Mobile Network, and turn the mobile data switch on. MMS needs an active mobile data connection, so this has to happen before picture messages will send.

MMS requires at least a 3G connection; 2G networks generally can't carry picture messages reliably. That's very likely a second reason your photos have been failing.

turns.thought:
I completely understand — you've done everything right so far, and it's reasonable to be frustrated. The good news is that your connection itself is now healthy: 5G, excellent signal, data and roaming on, SIM active. So the remaining causes are narrower. There are three things I'd check next, in order.

**1. APN settings — specifically the MMSC URL (most common remaining cause)**

MMS uses a dedicated server address called the MMSC URL, and it lives inside your APN settings. If it's missing or wrong, picture messages fail even with perfect data.

- Go to Settings → Network/Connections → Mobile Network → **Access Point Names (APN)**
- Check the MMSC / MMS URL field. If it is blank or doesn't look right, use **Reset to default** (usually in the three-dot menu)
- **Then reboot the device** — the reset won't take effect until you restart

**2. Wi-Fi Calling**

Even though your Wi-Fi is off, the Wi-Fi Calling setting can interfere with MMS on some configurations.

- Settings → Phone/Connections → **Wi-Fi Calling** → if it's ON, turn it **OFF**
- Try a picture message again

**3. Messaging app permissions**

The messaging app needs the storage permission (to attach the photo) and SMS permission (to send).

- Settings → Apps → your **messaging** app → **Permissions**
- Make sure **Storage** (or Photos/Videos) and **SMS** are both **Allowed/Granted**

Try a test picture message after each one so we can tell which change did it.

If none of those resolve it, I'll escalate you to technical support so they can run deeper diagnostics on the line — including the SIM-level checks that need their access. Since your last SIM replacement on this line was 2025-01-20, that's another angle they can look at.

Let me know what the APN/MMSC field shows, or how the test message goes.
